decision_rule.ADMITTED: the CI95 lower bound of the paired official pooled SLU-F1 delta (CELL-1-GEPA minus PLAN) is ABOVE ZERO and the CI95 lower bound of the paired intent delta exceeds -0.9943 (owner decision 99, the TRAIN lock: a gain is proven, not merely non-inferior)
decision_rule.DELTA_CONSUMPTION: item S3-4s: the per-node delta-consumption table -- how many deltas each node was supplied per row, which value_ids were supplied, and the saves and harms on the rows that received each one -- is a PRIMARY deliverable, reported whatever the verdict, placed beside CELL-1's own table, and is what decides whether there is a GEPA iteration 2 and what it retains. The PLANNER route is reported separately, never pooled: it grows from CELL-1's 14 values to 77 (73 of them GEPA-authored), and CELL-1 measured it at 0.594 of rows supplied and never at cap, so whether the route reaches its cap at all is this cell's own question. Each supplied value is also reported by PROVENANCE -- GEPA-authored or iteration-1 retained -- so the consumption table separates what the new statements did from what the kept ones did.
decision_rule.FRONTIER: owner decision 75: the frontier row (official SLU-F1 delta x prefilled tokens per row x GPU hours per 1,080 rows) is reported on every verdict and placed beside the registered rows.
decision_rule.HARMFUL: a MEASURED loss on either guard (owner decision 25, Method B: a CI95 upper bound below zero, or a point estimate beyond the margin); width alone is NEUTRAL, never HARMFUL
decision_rule.NEUTRAL: both guards are non-inferior -- the SLU CI95 lower bound exceeds -1.2485 and the intent CI95 lower bound exceeds -0.9943 -- without a proven SLU gain
decision_rule.PER_SCENARIO_HARM_BOUND: owner decision 17: per-scenario intent and SLU tables over all 18 scenarios in BOTH the natural-mixture and the equal-stratum weighting, with net harmed rows per scenario and any scenario of five or more flagged. A breach is a diagnostic beside the verdict, never a gate.
decision_rule.REPLICATION: an ADMITTED result is replicated on the SAME roster before any DEV, Fold B or test read (the owner iteration rule; no DEV read is authorised by this package).
decision_rule.SECOND_LOOK: CELL-1-GEPA is read on the same TRAIN Fold A rows whose CELL-1 read chose the retained set, so its verdict is a development number (owner decisions 28, 86) and never an independent confirmation; the replicate on the same roster and then on a fresh one (Fold B or DEV) precedes any effectiveness claim.
decision_rule.TWIN: ATTRIBUTION, never admission. The twin arm is read with the same estimator against the same sealed PLAN comparator. A gain the twin reproduces within the plan's own null is FORM (the store's shape and token volume), not content, and the verdict says so and claims no content effect. A gain the twin does not reproduce is attributed to the deltas' content, with the twin delta reported beside it.
decision_rule.comparator: the sealed PLAN arm SAEA-SLURP-NATIVE-DEFAULT-PLAN-LOCK-V1 (official 63.6304 / 82.2222); nothing is re-flown
decision_rule.efficiency_is_reported_regardless: every efficiency deliverable is reported whatever the verdict

The four baselines are CELL-1's with exactly three changes: the stage3-deltas release and snapshot pins moved to the stage3-deltas-gepa-v1 and stage3-deltas-gepa-twin-v1 namespaces, native_contact_fit renamed to this family's own GEPA-R01 identities, and prepared_phase_supply REMOVED (the cell-P0 form; the flip mints each cell's own artifact under its own run id, item E16). Every other decided key is byte-identical to CELL-1's -- and to CELL-2's -- so the one-factor proof against the locked plan still holds by construction and the three families' arms differ only in the store they pin (owner decision 101).

A recovery re-registration needs BOTH a new generation attempt id AND a new native_contact_fit.attempt_id in the baseline. CELL-1 lost two relaunches to exactly this: the fit gate binds the BASELINE's fit attempt id and refuses an identity that already carries evidence. Both failure_policy strings say so.

The two smoke FIT identities are declared as held CELLS in the smoke fragment, where CELL-1 left them undeclared (cell PLAN's form). Each of this family's eight run ids therefore carries a cell, a registered plan document, an exposure row and its own core.flight.cli check. This is the only intentional shape difference from CELL-1 and it authorises nothing extra: both cells stay held and are never flown as generation cells.

No decision requirement is registered in either fragment, on purpose: core.flight.repin._upsert_decision_requirement inserts the real one at the flip and a placeholder without an expected_decision_id would refuse the campaign at load.

FIRST-REQUEST BYTE IDENTITY, stated honestly before contact. Under this arm the first request of a row (Perception) is NOT byte-identical to the base's: the slot-contract cards it carries are the v2 release's (M4b). NATIVE TASK-CONTRACT CALL COUNT against the anchor's realized 1,082, and the count of tool calls emitted by a role that holds no authority (expected zero; a non-zero count is not a failure of the flight -- the rail refuses the call and the episode continues -- but it is the single most interesting behavioural consequence of showing three more roles the tool definitions, and it is reported per role).

PER-SCENARIO intent and SLU tables over all 18 scenarios, in BOTH the natural-mixture and the equal-scenario weighting, plus net harmed rows per scenario with any scenario of five or more flagged (owner decision 17) -- a diagnostic the verdict must carry, not an additional gate.

resume_recovery_clause: owner decision 22 of 2026-09-18. If an attempt dies of an INFRASTRUCTURE failure with code and request bytes unchanged -- never a harness or config defect -- the one allowed recovery may be a RESUME-RECOVERY under item E10 instead of a re-fly: every complete row of the aborted attempt is kept without selection, every partial or unstarted row is flown under the same run id, and the merged manifest declares the predecessor attempt with its trace hash, kept-row list and that list's hash. It changes no question, roster, factor, comparator, decision rule or cap, and the run-cumulative budget must be re-checked because a resumed attempt and its predecessor share one run id. A resumed EFFICIENCY read must additionally state the split of its GPU hours and prefilled tokens across attempts, because a merged manifest's cost is the sum of two lease windows and a per-row rate computed over the merged manifest alone would be wrong.
revisit_supply_rule: REGISTERED BEFORE CONTACT, and a correction of the rule CELL-2's driver carried: at a 448-value store a REVISE revisit acquires a SECOND, DISJOINT slice at each revisited node, because a candidate-bound route excludes what the accumulated QueryState already holds and then fills its cap from what is left. The offline dry run measures arm Solver 1 / Reviewer 4 / Planner 4 and twin Solver 4 / Reviewer 4 / Planner 0 on the second visit, with 25 (arm) and 24 (twin) distinct delta value ids over the episode and ZERO duplicate acquisitions. The invariant this cell registers is DISJOINTNESS, not emptiness: QueryState refuses a duplicate retrieved_value_id, EvidenceAgentController._acquired_ids refuses such a decision and the trajectory dies (the 2026-09-17 cell B1 abort). At CELL-2's 200-value store there was no second slice to find, so the two rules could not be told apart there. The consequence is a cost, not a defect: a revised row carries more delta text, which the E20 compaction count and the frontier row's token basis both report.
